Got stuff in your closet judging you? That jacket you swore you'd wear all the time? Boots that seemed genius at 2am online shopping? The impulse-buy disco pants now gathering dust?

Weird, normal, practical, chaotic, expensive, dirt cheap... if it's taking up space and someone else might love it, BRING IT.
One person's closet clutter is another's "holy shit where have you BEEN all my life?!"

THE DEAL: Fast fashion is literally destroying the planet, and community shouldn't cost you a credit card bill. This is about keeping good stuff circulating instead of rotting in landfills or feeding the Shein machine. Show up with your chaos, leave with someone else's chaos, make friends, eat snacks, and give clothing an actual second life.
No prerequisites. No dress code for entry. Just people sharing resources, fighting waste, and having a weird fun afternoon together.
RSVP REQUIRED — roll up with your bags of fabric regrets and an open mind.

content.text: Why does contemporary culture so often feel as though it has stopped producing genuinely new aesthetics?

In this lecture, given at Rutgers University in New Jersey, USA, artist, designer, writer, and professor Ruby Justice Thelot examines the conditions under which new forms emerge, and the economic, technological, and cultural forces that prevent them from reaching the mainstream.  Moving from the Beaux-Arts and Bauhaus to the Seagram Building, contemporary African architecture, Hollywood sequels, Pitchfork, video games, internet collage, experimental performance, fashion, and artificial intelligence, the lecture argues that aesthetic stagnation is not simply a failure of imagination. It is also the result of industrialization, financial risk aversion, algorithmic recommendation, and the growing weight of the cultural archive.

Ruby Justice Thelot is an artist, designer, researcher, and professor of design and media theory at NYU. His work focuses on digital phenomenology, virtual ontology, artificial intelligence, digital communities, and the implications of being online. He is the founder of the design and research studio 13101401 Inc. and the author of A Cyber Archaeology of Checkpoints and A Few Essays on Taste.
“We have a responsibility and a duty to make the future. Because if we don’t, somebody else will.”

content.text: Unusual Ventures & HumanSignal invite you to "Taste: A Physical AI Data Happy Hour"
Topic: The data machines can't make for themselves

Unusual Ventures and HumanSignal invite you to an evening of drinks, tastings, and real conversation with the people building physical AI, from frontier labs to robotics startups to the teams quietly running the data programs behind them.

Here's the premise. The hardest data in AI right now isn't online and can't be scraped. It has to be created in the physical world, from a first-person point of view, with human judgment in the loop. Teleoperation is hitting its ceiling. Simulation has its gap. The fastest-moving frontier is human and egocentric data, and the open question is how you create it, label it, and make it transfer.

So we're building the night around that idea: taste, judgment, and the signal only people can produce. Expect blind pisco and cocktail tastings, a few sensory challenges, and a DJ running human-made versus AI-generated tracks for the room to call. The games are the thesis: when can a model tell the difference, and when can only a person?
No slides, no pitch. Just the peers wrestling with the same problem, and a good excuse to compare notes. Come if you're leading AI work, building physical AI products, or running the data behind it.
Food, drinks, and tastings provided. Bring a plus-one.
Conversation we expect to get into:
Egocentric and first-person data: hype, or the real unlock
The human-to-robot embodiment gap, and what it takes to close it

After the passing of her adoptive parents, the orphan Oteru begins a solitary journey across mountains and wilderness to offer a lamp on Mount Kōya, praying for her parents and the people of her village.
A hundred miles of danger, carried by a single flame of devotion.
How will she withstand the storms of fate?
And how can one small lamp, once offered, shine without end?
孤女阿照在养父母离世后，只身翻山越岭前往高野山供灯，为养父母与乡亲祈福。
百里险途，一盏心灯相随。
她将如何穿越命运的风雨？
而那盏小小供灯，又如何得以长明不熄？
In ancient India, where the caste system casts long shadows, a humble barber hears rumour of a wisdom said to quiet suffering and open the gates of understanding.
Unfazed by mockery or status, he follows only the yearning of a heart seeking liberation.
Can someone born into poverty truly reach the vastness of real wisdom?
在等级森严的古印度，一位出身低微的理发师听闻世间有物，能息诸烦恼、启诸智慧。

content.text: We're living through a convergence of crises that is destabilizing society and our lives. AI and automation are rapidly reshaping labor and power. Climate change is accelerating, and as we write this, causing skyrocketing air pollution from wildfires and extreme heat waves. And underneath all this is an economic system that was never designed for the limits of a finite biosphere – a mismatch that's now driving political and social instability worldwide.
It's a lot to hold at once, and it's easy to feel overwhelmed. But what if these challenges share common roots, and a common path forward?
Climate Action Club is thrilled to host
for a conversation on his latest book

, which maps the crises of our time and the cognitive tools we'll need to move forward. Tom is an astrophysicist, designer, and executive who built products with global reach – including Microsoft Outlook, Yahoo Search, Google Glass, and Google's self-driving car program. After years supporting social entrepreneurs in the Global South working on access to clean water, electricity, education, and healthcare, he founded

: a VC that invests toward a world where humanity is net-positive to nature. Tom’s unique perspective –rooted in deep technical fluency and his understanding of the systems that shape our world – inform his thinking around how we can reclaim our agency and build the future we want: one where humanity and nature can flourish for generations to come.
